samples.summary: Self-removal leaves the user on a workspace page they no longer belong to; the invalidation refetch 403s into the error state
samples.evidence: `removeMemberMutation.onSuccess` (workspace-settings.tsx:134-139) always does `invalidateQueries({queryKey:['workspaces', workspaceId]})` and shows a success toast. The new frontend test (`workspace-settings.test.tsx:163-178`) exercises exactly the self-removal path for a non-owner: after `removeMember(slug, me.id)` succeeds, the caller is no longer a member, so the refetch of `fetchWorkspace(workspaceId)` returns 403 and the component falls into the `isError` branch (line 210-220) rendering "Failed to load workspace." instead of navigating the user away from the workspace. There is no navigate/redirect for the self-removal case, unlike `deleteMutation.onSuccess` which routes to a remaining workspace (lines 175-186).

samples.summary: revokeInvite resolves the workspace id twice (assertOwner already resolves), an extra DB round-trip per revoke
samples.evidence: `assertOwner(workspaceId, userId)` at line 138 already calls `resolveId(workspaceId)` internally (line 216); line 141 calls `resolveId` again, and the controller (workspace.controller.ts:109) has already resolved the slug to a UUID before calling the service. For a UUID the second call is a cheap no-op, but for a slug it is a redundant `workspace.findUnique`. Behaviourally harmless, just wasted work / duplicated resolution logic relative to `findInvites`/`createInvite`, which do not resolve at all.
